The Friedrich Schiller University Jena is a dynamic and innovation-driven university centrally located in Germany. With a broad range of disciplines, it shapes the future through excellent research and teaching. Its scientific excellence is reflected in the profile areas Light - Life - Liberty, which provide pioneering insights and sustainable solutions for the society of tomorrow. Through close collaborations with leading research institutions, innovative companies, and renowned cultural organizations, it advances interdisciplinary developments. With around 17,000 students and approximately 10,000 employees, it defines Jena as a vibrant, internationally connected city of science and innovation.The Chair of Glass Chemistry seeks to fill the position of aDoctoral research positionin the field of mechanoluminescent materialscommencing on January 1st, 2027, offered as fixed-term position for an initial period of 36 months according to TV-L E13 (75%).Mechanoluminescence (ML) is the fascinating phenomenon where a material emits light in response to mechanical stimuli, such as scratching, compression, or impact. By translating mechanical stress directly into a visible, infrared, or ultraviolet optical response, ML opens up a plethora of groundbreaking applications. These range from real-time damage monitoring in advanced structural materials to biophysical stress analysis and the visualization of acoustic waves.Despite its immense potential, the field of mechanoluminescence is still in its infancy. There is a critical gap both in the versatility of practical material solutions and in our fundamental understanding of the underlying physical and chemical mechanisms. knowledge of German is an asset but not mandatory.A cutting-edge research project at the forefront of materials science.Access to state-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure and characterization tools.Comprehensive mentoring and integration into a structured doctoral training program.A vibrant, international, and interdisciplinary research environment.Flexible working hours (flexitime and, if applicable, teleworking)A comprehensive further and continuing education programme and individual qualification and development measuresRemuneration based on the provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Sector of the Federal States (TV-L) at salary scale E13 - depending on the candidate’s personal qualifications-, including a special annual payment in accordance with the collective agreement.The posi...

jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for 1PhD Position in Developmental Psychology (75% position, E13 TV-L salary scale) – Starting January 1, 2027The Chair of Developmental Psychology at Ruhr-Universität Bochum invites applications for a position as a research associate (m/f/x) within a research project on the development of episodic memory in early childhood. The project will be conducted in close collaboration at two locations: Bochum and Dortmund. The successful candidate will contribute to the planning, execution, analysis, and publication of a longitudinal study involving children aged 3 to 5 years at the research site in Bochum. The project is embedded in a Collaborative Research Centre (CRC). The CRC “Episodic Memory” is an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework which conceptualizes scenarios as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information. As a member of this team, you will be trained in interdisciplinary research and have access to a broad spectrum of initiatives to support you in your academic journey. The CRC will be housed at the new research building THINK in Bochum, which is not only equipped with cutting edge technology, but also houses a childcare area (which includes, e.g., an outside play area, bedroom), parent child offices, common rooms to foster networking, etc. The position offers the opportunity for scientific qualification through a cumulative PhD. Patients benefit from the intensive interdisciplinary cooperation of 60 clinics and institutes. The particular strength of the university hospital lies in the close interlinking of clinical care and research for the safe application of new methods. At UKD, the medicine of tomorrow is created. Every day.The Institute of Pathology at Universitätsklinikum Düsseldorf (Director: Univ.-Prof. Dr. Irene Esposito), in a joint project with the Institute of Pharmaceutical Biology and Biotechnology (Prof. Dr. Nicole Teusch), is offering, at the earliest possible date, aPhD position (m/f/d)in the field of 3D Tumour Biology for Personalized Drug Discovery.Part-time, 65% of the weekly working hours.The appointment is initially limited to a period of 2 years, with the option of extension. This is a qualification position within the meaning of the German Act on Fixed-Term Employment Contracts in Academia (WissZeitVG, § 2 para. 1).Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest cancers, largely because its dense stromal and immune microenvironment drives therapy resistance that conventional cell-line models and 3D organoids fail to capture. jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for 1Doctoral Position (m,f,x) in Computational Neuroscience (Project Z02)Are you curious about how the human brain stores and retrieves memories? You want bridge the gap between academia and the wider public? The Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844) is an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework which conceptualizes scenarios as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information.We are actively seeking a talented PhD student to join our science communication project within the CRC 1844, which develops a digital serious game for citizen science, establishing a bidirectional bridge between episodic memory (EM) research and the general public. On the one hand, the game facilitates dissemination and intervention studies, with the public being involved in game design and extensions. On the other hand, the game allows for large-scale EM data collection from a diverse population. It also enables longitudinal research on EM, as well as prospective studies of EM changes preceding psychopathology.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030 (end of project)Start: from 01.01.2027, pending funding approvalApply by:  2026-11-02Your tasks:- The primary task will be the analysis of the behavioral data from gamified EM tasks, development of novel analyses, and interpretation of the results- Help adapt laboratory experiments into a serious game setting in collaboration with the Cologne Game Lab- Help validate the collected EM data in collaboration with experimental projects in the CRC 1844- Assist the outreach coordinator associated with this project with player recruitment and outreach activities- Correlate memory performance data from the game with demographic and psychological data in collaboration with the DZPG (German Center for Mental Health)- Engage in interdisciplinary collaborations with experimental and computational neuroscientists, psychologists, and philosophers- Present your results and findings in international conferences and scientific journalsYour profile:- An excellent master’s degree, or equivalent, in computational neuroscience, physics, mathematics, computer science, or a related field- Ability to work independently- Competence in mathematical modeling and statistical analysis- Excellent programming skills, e.g., Python- Relevant research experience in neuroscience or a related field- Excellent communication skills in English- Team spirit- Experience working within a collaborative research group (optional)https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/fec7155cf49f90ef54729f1412129f5b84aed4f70?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/fec7155cf49f90ef54729f1412129f5b84aed4f70?ref=AfA)

The Department of Pediatric Oncology, Hematology and Clinical Immunology at the University Hospital Düsseldorf (UKD) at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU), headed by Prof. Dr. Arndt Borkhardt, is one of the leading clinical centers for the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer in Germany. The clinic is part of the University Tumor Center (UTZ) at the UKD and the Center for Integrative Oncology Aachen-Bonn-Cologne-Düsseldorf (CIO-ABCD), which is funded by the German Cancer Aid. It is a founding partner of the German Consortium for Translational Cancer Research (DKTK) Essen-Düsseldorf and participates in international research consortia and study groups. The clinic operates a fully equipped research laboratory (safety level 1 and 2 according to the Genetic Engineering/Biotechnology Ordinance, including a GMP, next generation sequencing, flow cytometry, life cell imaging, and high-throughput drug testing facility) with 5 research groups and >30 staff working in an interdisciplinary manner on the fundamentals of childhood cancer and in the field of therapy optimization. We are seeking a highly motivated and creative PhD Student to join our research program in the field of amino acid homeostasis and cancer metabolism, with an anticipated start date of 02/2027. The successful candidate will work on the ERC-funded project “POWERFUL” (Deciphering how cancer cells fuel themselves to advance personalized treatment strategies).The PhD student will take a leading role in understanding how cancer cells sense and respond to amino acid availability, and how to translate this knowledge into precision-based treatment strategies. This position requires scientific independence and the opportunity to contribute intellectually to experimental design, data interpretation, and publication strategy. The candidate will employ and further develop advanced experimental models and methodologies, including organoid systems, patient-derived xenografts (PDXs), CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing, multiparameter flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, FRET assays, protein interaction and signaling assays, as well as in vitro and in vivo drug screening approaches.Candidates should have a very good understanding of and experience with standard molecular biology techniques including but not limited to tissue culture, genome editing, FACS analysis, confocal microscopy, immunoblot, and PCR/qPCR. Experience with animal models is a plus (as is FELASA B certification). Willingness to learn and work with murine experimental models is a fundamental requirement. - Master in natural sciences or related field- Solid experience with cancer models (e.g. organoids, PDXs) and drug-response studies- expertise in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including mammalian tissue culture, genome editing, FACS/flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, immunoblotting, and PCR/qPCR.- Excellent capability to develop new aspects and projects within the given research focus- Excellent written and spoken English language skills, German language skills are a plus- Organizational and project management experience- Willingness to cooperate and ability to work in a team- Experience in working with animals (FELASA B) is a plus, willingness to work with animals a requisite Remuneration is based on TV-L in pay grade 13 (65%), taking into account all previous periods of employment. The employment contract will be concluded with Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf.Applications from women are expressly welcome.
